sights.description: Museum in Ena dedicated to ukiyo-e artist Utagawa Hiroshige and his successors.

sights.description: A Gifu Prefecture natural monument, this roughly 300-year-old weeping cherry exceeds 20 meters in height and spread.

sights.name: Nitta Cherry Tree
sights.description: Over 450 years old and 24 meters tall, this giant Kohiganzakura stands in a private garden on high ground.

sights.name: Kamiyahagi Wind Power Plant
sights.description: Gifu Prefecture's first wind farm began operating in June 2007, with 13 turbines about 1,100 meters up.

sights.name: Iwamura Historical Museum
sights.description: A history museum on the Iwamura domain lord's former residence, at the foot of Iwamura Castle ruins.

sights.name: Ena Gin no Mori
sights.description: This complex, surrounded by seasonal nature, offers tasty experiences.

sights.name: Benkei Cedar
sights.description: In the Tenpyo era, Todaiji high priest Roben climbed the mountain, recited the Lotus Sutra, and founded Kakurinbo.

sights.name: Enakyo Sazanami Plaza Cherry Blossoms
sights.name_en: Ena Gorge Sazanami Plaza Cherry Blossoms
sights.description: During bloom, Ena Gorge Park's Sazanami Plaza is lit from sunset until 10 p.m., best viewed early to mid-April.

sights.name: Ryugo-ji Temple
sights.description: Ryugoji, family temple of the Akechi Toyama clan, has Akechi Mitsuhide's memorial tower, split by a large diagonal crack.

sights.name: Ochiai Fort (Senjojiki Park)
sights.description: Ochiai Fort, said to predate Akechi Castle built in 1247, is now Senjojiki Park with good views from its outwork.

sights.name: Grave of Omaki no Kata
sights.description: Grave of Omaki no Kata, Akechi Mitsuhide's mother, offered as a hostage when Yakami Castle would not fall in 1575.

sights.name: Tengu Shrine and Mitsuhide Study Site
sights.name_en: Lord Akechi Mitsuhide's Study Hall and Tenjin Shrine
sights.description: In Mangahora, young Akechi Mitsuhide is said to have studied under a Tenryu-ji monk at this shrine to Sugawara no Michizane.

sights.name: Kinheisha Hachioji Shrine
sights.description: Founded in the Heian period, its 1678 hall is a prefectural Important Cultural Property; the karamon was reportedly moved from Akechi Castle.

sights.name: Akechi Castle Ruins
sights.description: A mountain castle in southern Ena, second in scale to Iwamura Castle and the Akechi Toyama clan's successive seat.

sights.name: Sakaori Rice Terraces
sights.name_en: NPO Ena City Sakaori Rice Terrace Preservation Society
sights.description: This society conserves Ena's Sakaori rice terraces, selected among Japan's 100 best, and seeks to revitalize mountain farming.

sights.name: Kori River Dam
sights.description: A multipurpose dam on the Ena-Mizunami border for flood control, river conservation, and power generation, with its interior open to visitors.

sights.name: Iwamura Brewery
sights.description: Sake brewery in Iwamura, Ena, offering tours and tastings of local rice wine.

sights.name: Taisho-mura Roman-tei
sights.description: Taisho-era museum in Ena showcasing early 20th-century culture and design.

sights.name: Former Miyake House
sights.description: An Ena City designated cultural property, donated in 1991 and relocated and restored the following year.

sights.name: Former Akechi Town Hall
sights.name_en: Nihon Taisho-mura Village Hall (Former Akechi Town Hall)
sights.description: Built in 1906, this ultra-modern two-story wooden Western-style hall served as Akechi Town Hall until 1957 and was designated a tangible cultural property in 1999.

sights.name: Ukare Yokocho
sights.description: Part of the Chuma Kaido, this nostalgic alley once had sake and udon shops for travelers and packhorse drivers, and some houses span the road.

sights.name: Nakatsugawa-Shinshu Kaido Crossing
sights.name_en: Old Highways Crossing (Chuma Kaido and Nanboku Kaido)
sights.description: This Akechi crossing of the Chuma and Nanboku Kaido, once busy with packhorse drivers and Ise pilgrims, led toward Shiojiri, Owari, Okazaki, and the Nakasendo.

sights.name: Maple Planted by Akechi Mitsuhide
sights.description: Tradition says Lord Mitsuhide enshrined Hitomaro at Hachioji Shrine and planted this maple before the Kakinomoto no Hitomaro Shrine.

sights.name: Ishikawa Tomato Farm
sights.description: Ishikawa Tomato Farm grows tomatoes at 650 meters in Kamiyahagi using Yahagi River headwaters, and sells them by mail order.

sights.name: Enakyo Gorge Cherry Blossoms
sights.description: Geographer Shiga Shigetaka named this gorge in 1920; about 200 cherry trees bloom each spring at Sazanami Plaza in Ena Gorge Park.

sights.name: Mansho-ji Temple
sights.description: A hidden Senju Kannon said to be made by Jikaku Daishi Ennin is enshrined here and revered locally for warding off misfortune.

sights.name: Meiji Emperor's Rest House Ooi
sights.name_en: Emperor Meiji's Oi Lodging on the Nakasendo
sights.description: The former Ito inn at Oi-juku on the Nakasendo lodged Emperor Meiji in 1880 and still preserves its rooms, bath, and toilet.

sights.name: Kakashi Street
sights.description: Varied, realistic scarecrows stand near the Kiriyama bus stop in Kasagi-cho's Himeguri district, an area called Scarecrow Street.

sights.name: Nakasendo Ooi-juku
sights.description: Historic post town on the Nakasendo, once the busiest station in Gifu Prefecture.

sights.name: Hishiya Archives
sights.description: Typical grand townhouse of the Furuyama family, leading Oi-juku merchants and village headmen from the mid-Edo period.

sights.name: Iwamura Basin Farmhouses
sights.description: Traditional tiled, white-walled farmhouses and storehouses scatter across the gently sloping Iwamura Basin, framed by hills and mountains.

sights.name: Katsukawa Residence
sights.description: Late-Edo merchant house known as Matsuya, comprising two wooden two-story buildings, opened in August 2003.

sights.name: Iwamura Castle Site Park
sights.name_en: Castle Ruins Park (Drum Turret, Shimoda Utako Study Hall, Chishin Hall)
sights.description: Park on about two hectares of former samurai land below Iwamura Castle, with a museum, drum turret, and study hall.

sights.name: Iibama Castle Ruins
sights.description: Ruins of a small Iwamura branch castle of the Toyama Iibama clan, said to have linked defenses with Naegi and Akechi.

sights.name: Kimura Residence
sights.description: Imposing townhouse of the Kimura family, a former wholesaler on Iwamura castle town's main street, prosperous from mid to late Edo.

sights.name: Tosaya
sights.description: Dyeing merchant house from about 260 years ago, restored and opened in April 1999 as the Tosaya crafts hall.

sights.name: Kano House
sights.description: An Ena City-designated cultural property, the Kano family of Iwamura domain gunsmiths displays gunsmith tools.

sights.name: Iwamura Art Museum
sights.description: The typical Meiji-era Shibata House opened in 2003 as an art museum showing paintings, including works by Harada Hoshu.

sights.name: Kasagi Gorge
sights.description: The Kiso River gorge and lake formed by Kasagi Dam, downstream of Oi Dam, are famous for autumn foliage.

sights.name: Tatsubara Gorge
sights.description: The upper Kamimura River, a first-class river in Gifu's Yahagi system, forms a steep gorge of green mountains and clear water.

sights.name: Saigyo no Mori
sights.description: Planted in 1989 for the city's 35th anniversary, this 14.8-hectare forest holds 136 trees of 100 cherry varieties.

sights.name: Tozan Cherry Tree
sights.description: An old higan cherry along the Akechi River, in the former hatamoto Toyama residence, came to be called Toyama Cherry.

sights.name: Gomozaza
sights.description: A wooden local playhouse and community hall built in 1951, nationally registered as tangible cultural property in 2010.

sights.name: Yamaoka Station Kantenkan
sights.description: A food-and-health station in Yamaoka-cho, Ena, with an agar museum, agar restaurant, and agar product manufacturing and sales.

sights.name: Ichiyajo Castle Ruins
sights.description: A fort on a mountain overlooking Akechi, said to be where Takeda Katsuyori camped in a Tensho 2 battle.

sights.name: Okuyahagi Lake Cherry Avenue
sights.description: In Kushihara, Ena, over a thousand Somei-Yoshino bloom along the lake, partly forming a tunnel; best from early to mid-April.

sights.name: Hazama Fudoson

sights.name: Nichiryubuji Temple (Takazawa Kannon)

sights.name: Oni ga Otoshita Oishi

sights.name: Shin-Chokokuji Temple (Kita Kannon)

sights.name: Koga Shrine

sights.name: Iwato no Taki

sights.name: Kasuga Shrine

sights.name: Momijibafu and Tokaede Tree-Lined Road

sights.description: For about 4 km from Wakakusa Tunnel toward Seki Techno Highland and north of City Hall, Momijibafu and Tokaede turn red and yellow in autumn.

sights.name: Teraogahara Senbonzakura Park
sights.name_en: Autumn Leaves at Teraogahara Senbonzakura Park
sights.description: This park, known for full spring cherry blossoms, also shows striking autumn color as trees along about 2 km of road turn red and orange.

sights.name: Kasuga Shrine Autumn Leaves
sights.description: Beloved as guardian of Seki swordsmiths, Kasuga Shrine has maples and ginkgo that turn red and yellow along the approach and Noh stage in autumn.

sights.name: Mirokuji
sights.description: Miroku-ji in Ikejiri, Seki, is known for ties to Edo-period monk Enku, who is said to have spent his later years here.

sights.name: Seki Zenkoji

sights.name: Mirokuji Cherry Blossoms

sights.name: Gifu Prefectural Hyakunen Park

activities.name: Sekigahara Oshi Trip – Role-Play Journey

sights.name: Sekigahara Battlefield
sights.description: Amid the fields, stone monuments and Tokugawa and Ishida crest flags stand where Sekigahara fighting was especially fierce.

sights.name: Mount Ibuki Driveway
sights.description: A 17 km automobile-only road spanning Shiga and Gifu climbs near the 1,377-meter summit of Mount Ibuki, one of Japan's 100 famous mountains.

sights.name: Gifu Sekigahara Battlefield Memorial Museum
sights.name_en: Gifu Sekigahara Historic Battlefield Memorial Museum
sights.description: Opened in October 2020 in Sekigahara, this hands-on museum uses the latest technology so visitors can understand the whole 1600 battle.

sights.name: Sekigahara War Land
sights.description: Asano Shoun's 200-plus concrete figures recreate the Sekigahara battle, including Tokugawa Ieyasu, Ishida Mitsunari, gun squads, and foot soldiers.

sights.name: Mount Ibuki Driveway Autumn Foliage
sights.description: Mount Ibuki is the recommended autumn-leaf spot in Sekigahara; trail kusamomiji maples start coloring from around early October.

sights.name: Tokugawa Ieyasu Final Camp Site
sights.name_en: Tokugawa Ieyasu's Final Camp Site and Shogiba
sights.description: Around 11 a.m. on the day of the battle, Tokugawa Ieyasu moved his headquarters here from Momokubariyama to face Ishida Mitsunari's camp.

sights.name: Sekigahara Battlefield Decisive Ground
sights.name_en: Sekigahara Historic Battlefield Decisive Battle Site
sights.description: On the morning of September 15, 1600, Kobayakawa Hideaki's betrayal turned the Western advantage into an Eastern Army victory.

sights.name: Otani Yoshitsugu Monument
sights.description: Erected in 1940 by the Fuwa Historic Sites Preservation Society, it presents Otani Yoshitsugu's end as a model of bushido.

sights.name: Sekigahara Limestone Cave
sights.description: The cave stays about 15 degrees, with stalagmites, rainbow trout in spring water, and Paleozoic fossils; the 518-meter route takes about 20 minutes.

sights.name: Sasao-yama Ishida Mitsunari Camp Site
sights.name_en: Ishida Mitsunari Camp Site on Sasaoyama
sights.description: Ishida Mitsunari, Western Army commander, camped on Sasaoyama the day before the battle to overlook Sekigahara and hold the Hokkoku Kaido.

sights.name: Myo-oji Temple
sights.description: Founded in 1360 by Nagae Shigekage for his late mother, it is the prefecture's oldest Soto Zen temple.

sights.name: Hosokawa Tadaoki Jin-ato
sights.description: Hosokawa Tadaoki, one of Sen no Rikyu's seven disciples, joined the Eastern Army at Sekigahara from the start.

sights.name: Momohai-yama Tokugawa Ieyasu Jin-ato
sights.name_en: Momokubariyama, Tokugawa Ieyasu's First Camp Site
sights.description: Eastern Army commander-in-chief Tokugawa Ieyasu deployed at Momokubariyama on the morning of September 15, 1600.

sights.name: Sekigahara Kessenjo Kaisenchi
sights.description: The Battle of Sekigahara opened here when Fukushima Masanori volleyed after the Ii unit fired early.

sights.name: Otani Yoshitsugu Grave and Yuasa Gonsuke Grave
sights.name_en: Graves of Otani Yoshitsugu and Yuasa Gosuke
sights.description: Otani Yoshitsugu's grave stands quietly with aide Yuasa Gosuke's, a 15-minute climb from Hiratsuka Tamehiro's monument.

sights.name: Matsudaira Tadachika Ii Naomasa Jin-ato
sights.name_en: Matsudaira Tadayoshi and Ii Naomasa Camp Site
sights.description: Ii Naomasa wanted his son-in-law Matsudaira Tadayoshi, Ieyasu's fourth son, to earn merit in his first battle.

sights.name: Otani Yoshitsugu Jin-ato
sights.description: Otani's camp, begun about ten days before the battle above Wakamiya Hachimangu, had dry moats on both sides.

sights.name: Matsuo-yama Castle Ruins Kobayakawa Hideaki Jin-ato
sights.name_en: Matsuo Yama Castle Ruins and Kobayakawa Hideaki Camp Site
sights.description: Matsuo Yama Castle is famous as the mountain castle where Kobayakawa Hideaki deployed his forces.

sights.name: Sekigahara Town History and Folklore Museum
sights.name_en: Sekigahara Town History and Folklore Learning Center
sights.description: Renewed in October 2020, it focuses on Sekigahara Town's local history with educational and hands-on elements.

sights.name: Shimazu Yoshihiro Jin-ato
sights.name_en: Shimazu Yoshihiro Camp Site (Shimazu Retreat Site)
sights.description: The Shimazu Yoshihiro camp site lies behind Shinmei Shrine, near the center of the Western Army positions.

sights.name: Okayama Beacon Hill
sights.name_en: Kuroda Nagamasa and Takenaka Shigekado Camp Site / Okayama (Maruyama) Beacon Site
sights.description: On 164-meter Okayama hill, Takenaka Shigekado and Kuroda Nagamasa camped and raised Sekigahara's opening beacon.

sights.name: Myojin no Mori
sights.description: North of the old battlefield beside Mount Ibuki, Myojin Forest offers seasonal flowers and wonderful views.

sights.name: Higashi Kubizuka
sights.description: Just west of JR Sekigahara Station, Higashi Kubizuka is in a broadleaf forest beyond a large vermilion gate.

sights.name: Yamauchi Kazutoyo Jin-ato
sights.description: Along the old Nakasendo, the camp site is marked by a large pine and the Yamauchi oak-leaf war banner.

sights.name: Shima Sakon Jin-ato
sights.description: Called too good for Mitsunari, Shima Sakon camped at the foot of Mount Sasao and repeatedly repelled Eastern Army attacks.

sights.name: Honda Tadakatsu Jin-ato
sights.description: Honda Tadakatsu, one of Tokugawa's Four Heavenly Kings, was a brave, strategic general also loved by his domain's people.

sights.name: Ukita Hideie Jin-ato
sights.description: Tenman Shrine stands at the foot of cedar-covered Nantenmanzan, where Ukita Hideie deployed about 17,000 Western troops.

sights.name: Shoren-ji Yatsufusa-ume
sights.description: Shorenji Temple in Hirai, Imasu, has the Yatsufusa plum, a natural monument designated by the town and prefecture.

sights.name: Tanaka Yoshimasa Jin-ato
sights.description: The monument stands beside Tokugawa Ieyasu's final camp and was moved to Jinbano in 1987.

sights.name: Fukushima Masanori Jin-ato
sights.description: His camp remains at Kasuga Shrine with the 800-year-old Tsukimi-no-miya cedar depicted in the Sekigahara battle screen.

sights.name: Konishi Yukinaga Camp Site
sights.description: Konishi Yukinaga deployed about 6,000 Western Army troops at Hokutenmanzan and raised a signal fire for his allies.

sights.name: Hiratsuka Tamekuni Monument
sights.description: It stands east of the road downhill from the Otani Yoshitsugu camp site.

sights.name: Nishi Kubizuka
sights.description: Takenaka Shigekado buried soldiers killed in the Battle of Sekigahara here on Tokugawa Ieyasu's orders.

sights.name: Satsuma-ike Pond
sights.description: A small pond used militarily by Shimazu Yoshihiro's troops, said never to have dried since ancient times.

sights.name: Todo Takatora & Kyogoku Takatomo Camp Site
sights.name_en: Todo Takatora and Kyogoku Takatomo Camp Site
sights.description: Todo Takatora and Kyogoku Takatomo reportedly camped on present-day Sekigahara Junior High School grounds.

sights.name: Wakizaka Yasuharu Camp Site
sights.description: It lies at the foot of Mt. Matsuo, between the Meishin Expressway and Kurochi River.

sights.name: Fujikogawa Fireflies
sights.description: From early to mid-June, Genji fireflies can be seen around Fujiko River, sometimes hundreds at once.

sights.name: Hissui Gorge Rock Azalea

sights.name: Bodai Yama Castle Ruins
sights.description: Hilltop castle ruins in Tarui with a 2.7 km hiking trail to 402-metre summit.

sights.name: Nangu Taisha
sights.description: Mino Province's chief shrine, it enshrines mine deity Kanayamahiko and has long been the head shrine of Japan's mining and metal industries.

sights.name: Takenaka Shi Jinya Ato
sights.description: Ruins of the residence of Takenaka Shigekado, son of the strategist Takenaka Hanbei, in Tarui.

sights.name: Zendo-ji
sights.description: Hanbei's son Shigekado moved his grave here after Takenaka Hanbei died of illness at age 36 in 1579.

sights.name: Mori Hidemoto Jinseki
sights.description: At Sekigahara, Mori Hidemoto camped on Mount Nangu for the Western Army but could not fight due to Kikkawa Hiroie's collusion.

sights.name: Chosokabe Morichika Jinseki
sights.description: Chosokabe Morichika camped on Mount Nangu for the Western Army but withdrew without fighting when the Mori army did not move.

sights.name: Tarui Castle Ruins
sights.description: Hiratsuka Tamehiro, lord of Tarui Castle, fought for the Western Army under Otani Yoshitsugu at Sekigahara.

sights.name: Kurihara Ninety-nine Temples Ruins
sights.name_en: Kurihara Tsukumobo Site (Chosokabe Morichika Camp Site)
sights.description: A large temple complex spreading from the summit of Mount Kurihara to its eastern foothills.

sights.name: Tarui History and Folk Museum
sights.name_en: Taruipia Center History and Folklore Museum
sights.description: Covers Takenaka Hanbei and Tarui-juku, the lively Nakasendo-Minoji junction, plus a recreated burial-mound chamber.

sights.name: Yoshikawa Hiroie Encampment Site
sights.description: As clan eldest, he opposed Mori Hidemoto joining the Western army, secretly contacted Ieyasu, and camped on Mount Nangu.

sights.name: Nakasendo-Minoji Tarui Fork Signpost
sights.name_en: Nakasendo and Minoji Tarui Oiwake Guidepost
sights.description: Built in 1709, this guidepost marks the Nakasendo-Minoji junction and is the seventh oldest of over 250.

sights.name: Ikeda Terumasa Camp Site and Haruo-Yasuo Graves
sights.description: Terumasa camped facing Mount Nangu's forces; his monument shares the site of the Muromachi-period Haruo and Yasuo graves.

sights.name: Aikawa Riverside Park Cherry Blossoms
sights.description: About 200 Somei-Yoshino cherries over 50 years old bloom along the Aikawa from late March to early April.

sights.name: Ankokuji Keian Encampment Site
sights.description: Ankokuji Ekei camped on Mt. Nangu for the Western Army at Sekigahara and was later beheaded in Kyoto.

sights.name: Natsuka Masaie Encampment Site
sights.description: Nagatsuka Masaie, one of Hideyoshi's five commissioners, camped on Mt. Nangu but withdrew to Minakuchi without fighting.

sights.name: Asakura-yama Shinzen-in
sights.description: A Tendai temple founded in 739, with a three-story pagoda and bell said to be the prefecture's oldest, both Important Cultural Properties.

sights.name: Tarui Ichirizuka
sights.description: In 1604 Ieyasu ordered milestones; Tarui's is one of only two nationally designated ones on the Nakasendo.

sights.name: Minoji Pine Avenue
sights.description: Starting point of Minoji, an important side road linking the Nakasendo and Tokaido, about 57.5 km from Tarui-juku to Miya-juku.

sights.name: Asano Yoshinaga Camp Site
sights.description: Asano Yoshinaga, eldest son of Asano Nagamasa, joined the Eastern Army at Sekigahara as vanguard and captured Gifu Castle.
